title: The Pentagon Directs $2B to Stockpile Critical Minerals, Manila Seeks Bespoke Indian BrahMos Missiles, and ASELSAN Signs a $1.1B Air Defense Export Contract
subhead: The US Defense Logistics Agency is deploying $2 billion to build Cold War-scale reserves of critical minerals even as supply bottlenecks and a new Democratic Congress cloud President Trump's $1.5 trillion defense budget request. In Asia, the Philippines opened talks with India for terrain-adapted BrahMos supersonic missiles as an alternative to stretched US supply lines, South Korea's Hanwha committed $50 million to military robot dogs, and Turkey's ASELSAN signed a $1.1 billion single-item air defense export contract.

sections.heading: Pentagon Commits $2B to Critical Mineral Stockpiles as Midterms Imperil $1.5T Defense Budget
sections.body:
The Pentagon's Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) has directed $2 billion to acquire and stockpile critical minerals and strategic materials in a reserve expansion officials compared to Cold War-era mobilization programs, though Fortune reported the effort is already running into global mining and processing bottlenecks (Defence Industry Europe, Fortune). At the same time, private equity firm Apollo Global Management published an assessment framing NATO's multi-year defense industrial buildout as a major deployment opportunity for private capital.

However, the political ceiling for US military spending shifted abruptly after Tuesday's midterm elections. According to Bloomberg and Defense One, the Democratic sweep of Congress has effectively extinguished prospects for President Donald Trump's $1.5 trillion defense budget proposal, subjecting major Pentagon procurement programs and defense contractors to heightened congressional scrutiny and potential spending caps in 2027.
sections.whyItMatters: While the Pentagon is trying to lock in $2 billion of raw materials for munitions and electronics, the incoming Democratic House majority is poised to cap top-line defense appropriations well below the White House's $1.5 trillion target.

sections.heading: Philippines Seeks Terrain-Adapted Indian BrahMos Missiles as Hanwha and Renault Bet on Combat Robotics
sections.body:
The Philippines is negotiating with India to purchase additional BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles customized for archipelagic and island terrain, a move analysts told the South China Morning Post reflects Manila's effort to diversify its weapons suppliers while US defense production remains tied down by the eight-month conflict in the Middle East (SCMP).

Across Northeast Asia and Europe, defense primes and automakers are accelerating investments in unmanned ground systems. South Korean defense conglomerate Hanwha committed $50 million to develop military quadruped 'robot dogs,' intensifying South Korea's domestic defense robotics race, while French automaker Renault announced plans to enter the military robotics manufacturing business (A3 Association for Advancing Automation, Electrek). Meanwhile, along the inter-Korean border, more than 13,000 visitors flocked to South Korea's Aegibong Peace Ecopark in Gimpo over a 10-day period after a North Korean self-propelled howitzer became clearly visible from the observatory (SCMP).
sections.whyItMatters: Manila's push for customized Indian supersonic missiles shows US allies in the First Island Chain actively hedging against American munition backlogs by turning to Asian defense producers.

sections.heading: ASELSAN Signs $1.1B Air Defense Export Deal and TUSAŞ Delivers HÜRKUŞ-II Trainers
sections.body:
Turkish defense electronics leader ASELSAN signed a historic single-item export contract worth $1.1 billion for air defense systems, marking one of the largest standalone air defense export agreements in the company's history, while also announcing a solar power plant investment to supply 100 percent of its electricity consumption from renewable energy (Envanter Medya, DonanımHaber, CNN Türk).

In military aviation, Turkish Aerospace Industries (TUSAŞ) delivered the third and fourth HÜRKUŞ-II next-generation basic trainer aircraft from Mürted Air Base in Ankara to the Turkish Air Force's 2nd Main Jet Base Command in Çiğli, İzmir, following the initial two deliveries in September (Tolga Özbek). Meanwhile, Ankara's defense industry cluster announced an expansion adding 70 new defense firms with a target of creating 40,000 jobs, while Turkish defense companies showcased unmanned aerial and autonomous systems in Bangkok and held talent recruitment meetings with engineers in Munich (TRT Haber, Anadolu Agency, ssbulten.com.tr). Separately, Nordic Monitor published a report examining links between Turkey's spaceport facility in Somalia and long-range missile testing infrastructure.
sections.whyItMatters: A $1.1 billion single-item air defense export contract demonstrates that Turkish defense firms are moving from selling individual tactical drones and armored vehicles to exporting integrated, high-ticket air defense architectures.

sections.heading: CENTCOM Stands Up 'Iron Gate' Task Force as Drone Hits Iraq's Khor Mor Gas Field
sections.body:
Following Saturday's announcement of a land-route interdiction mission, US Central Command formally designated the operation as Task Force 'Iron Gate', aimed at severing Iranian ground supply corridors across the Middle East (Al Jazeera, Yeni Şafak). Late Sunday, an explosive drone struck the Khor Mor gas facility in northern Iraq's Sulaymaniyah province, halting gas production and cutting electricity to more than 70 percent of Iraq's Kurdish region (Al Jazeera, Star). Even so, President Donald Trump stated that fresh direct US military strikes on Iran are 'unlikely' and maintained that Tehran remains open to a deal, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the war as necessary to prevent a nuclear threat (Reuters, AP News, Anadolu Agency).

In Yemen, government forces reported conducting 992 operations that killed or wounded 267 Houthi fighters while losing nine officers, as Houthi authorities in Sanaa said Saudi airstrikes on the Yemeni capital killed 44 people and injured 40 (Anadolu Agency). In southern Lebanon, the Israeli military continued artillery shelling and house demolitions across border towns (Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: While Task Force Iron Gate aims to seal overland weapons routes into the Levant, the strike on Khor Mor shows armed groups in Iraq can retaliate immediately against civilian power infrastructure.

sections.heading: Russian Strikes Cut Power to 600,000 Ukrainian Homes and Disconnect Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant
sections.body:
Russian missile and drone strikes targeted electrical substations supplying Ukraine's defense industry in the Dnipro and Zhytomyr regions as well as port infrastructure, leaving 600,000 households without electricity, while Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha reported that the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant lost its external power supply for the 16th time this year (Yeni Şafak, Anadolu Agency).

On the cyber front, two hacking groups — Silent Crown and Belarus Cyber Partisans — claimed responsibility for breaching Russia's state statistics agency Rosstat, alleging that leaked internal records point to at least 390,000 Russian military deaths in the conflict (The Independent).
sections.whyItMatters: Targeting substations tied specifically to defense manufacturing in Dnipro and Zhytomyr while repeatedly severing external grid links to Zaporizhzhia increases nuclear safety and industrial disruption risks as winter temperatures drop.

bottomLine: Defense industrial bottlenecks and post-midterm budget limits dominated Monday's defense brief: the Pentagon's Defense Logistics Agency committed $2 billion to stockpile critical minerals on a Cold War scale, even as a new Democratic Congress prepares to block President Trump's $1.5 trillion defense budget request. In the Indo-Pacific and Middle East, US allies and regional powers are moving quickly to expand their own production and supplier networks — the Philippines is seeking customized BrahMos missiles from India, South Korea's Hanwha is investing $50 million in military robot dogs, French automaker Renault is entering military robotics, and Turkey's ASELSAN closed a $1.1 billion single-item air defense export contract. On active fronts, CENTCOM launched Task Force 'Iron Gate' as a drone strike knocked out northern Iraq's Khor Mor gas field, while Russian strikes cut power to 600,000 Ukrainian homes and severed external power to the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant for the 16th time this year.
